cancel_basis: Flightradar24 RUH board count: departures + arrivals scheduled on the local day (midnight to midnight, Riyadh time), including flights still to come, identical rows de-duplicated. Percent = share of flights scheduled today.

report.title: RUH Airport Status 12:00 AM AST: DISRUPTED
report.status_line: Day total for 9 October; traffic has been moving since 9:38 PM.
report.headline: 9 October totals: 166 flights cancelled at RUH and four halts of 45+ minutes, the longest 7:41 to 9:38 PM; traffic moving again since 9:38 PM.
report.synopsis: There were 13 takeoffs in the last hour, the latest XY53 to Jeddah at 11:42 PM. The latest landing was F3236 from Madinah at 11:38 PM, with 8 landings in the last hour. 166 flights are cancelled on 9 October (72 departures, 94 arrivals) and 18 arrivals have diverted. 9 October in review: RUH had halts of 45 minutes or more at 5:32 to 6:24 AM, 1:58 to 3:14 PM, 4:05 to 4:50 PM and 7:41 to 9:38 PM (no landing 7:41 to 9:45 PM), plus a shorter midday pause. The evening stop drove most of the day’s diversions, mainly to Madinah and Qassim. GACA, via Al Arabiya, said three people were killed in two attacks on the airport; no official reason has been given for the evening stop.
report.gulf_footnote: Riyadh Air RX243 to Dubai, due 3:50 PM, finally left at 9:50 PM. Cancelled today include Emirates EK816, EK820, EK818, flydubai FZ848, FZ842, FZ856 and flynas XY217 to Dubai; Qatar Airways QR1167, QR1171, QR1241, QR1169, QR1165, QR1239 and QR1173 to Doha; Etihad EY552, EY556 and EY560 to Abu Dhabi; SalamAir OV206 to Muscat.
report.news_title: Traffic resumes after the 7:41 to 9:45 PM stop with no official reason; Mauritania and the UN envoy condemn the airport attacks.

news.title: UAE condemns the Houthi attacks on King Khalid airport and a Saudia aircraft, which killed three Saudis
news.body: The UAE Foreign Ministry condemned the Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport and a Saudia aircraft, which killed three Saudis, calling them a blatant violation of Saudi sovereignty. Al Ekhbariya also reported the condemnation at 10:38 PM (https://x.com/alekhbariyaNews/status/2108643190026932411). No operational information.

news.title: UN envoy for Yemen and Mauritania condemn the Houthi attacks on King Khalid and Abha airports
news.body: SPA reports Mauritania condemned the attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport. At 10:12 PM Al Ekhbariya reported the UN special envoy for Yemen also condemned the attacks on both airports (https://x.com/alekhbariyaNews/status/2108636663836803288). Neither gives an operational reason for the evening halt.

news.title: Flightradar24: many flights diverting to alternate airfields, then flights now making their way toward Riyadh
news.extra: posts 8:50, 9:20 and 9:31 PM; last checked 9:33 PM
news.body: At 9:20 PM Flightradar24 posted that many flights were diverting to alternate airfields (https://x.com/flightradar24/status/2108623703919763526); at 9:31 PM it said flights are now making their way toward Riyadh. At 8:50 PM it noted the last landing was over an hour ago (https://x.com/flightradar24/status/2108616180432814231). The board matches: 9 diversions during the stop, no landing yet after 7:41 PM.

news.title: teleSUR says Houthi spokesman Saree claimed a ballistic missile attack on Riyadh airport; no matching Saree post found
news.body: teleSUR English reports that Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed a ballistic missile attack on King Khalid International Airport. We found no matching post on Saree's own account. The Ministry of Defense, SPA and Reuters had said nothing as of 9:11 PM.

news.title: France and Syria condemn the Houthi attacks; Syria names King Khalid airport
news.body: Saudi state TV Al Ekhbariya reports France condemned the Houthi attacks on civilian sites in the Kingdom and expressed solidarity. At 8:22 PM it reported Syria condemned the attacks on King Khalid International Airport (https://x.com/alekhbariyaNews/status/2108609076263354737). Neither gives operational information.

news.title: Posts call this Riyadh’s fifth closure today
news.body: A user post says Riyadh closed for the fifth time today and aircraft are holding, with some diverting low on fuel. Our board-based count shows this is the fourth halt of 45+ minutes today (5:32 AM, 1:58 PM, 4:05 PM, 7:41 PM).

news.title: Posts report explosions or sirens in Riyadh from 8:18 to 8:44 PM, and aircraft holding; no official confirmation
news.body: Several social accounts reported explosions or sirens in Riyadh between about 8:18 and 8:44 PM, and air traffic holding near the city (e.g. https://x.com/PeterVogel/status/2108609212096094356). No official confirmation.

news.title: Houthi spokesman claims Saudi jets carried out 77 air and missile strikes in Yemen in 24 hours
news.body: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed Saudi warplanes carried out 77 air strikes and missile attacks on Sanaa and several provinces in the past 24 hours, using aircraft from Khamis Mushait and Taif. This is a Houthi claim, not independently confirmed; it says nothing about RUH.

news.title: Civil Defense warns against filming or sharing interception or debris sites; no shelter order
news.body: Saudi Civil Defense warned the public not to film or share interception or debris sites. It did not issue a shelter order.

news.title: Superseded: GACA (via Al Arabiya) said three were killed in two attacks and operations had returned to normal; traffic stopped again at 7:41 PM
news.body: Al Arabiya English reports, citing the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA), that three people were killed in two attacks on Riyadh airport and that operations have returned to normal. BasNews English (8:10 PM, https://x.com/EnglishBasNews/status/2108605958532268527) also cites GACA for the three deaths and says one of the two attacks hit a Saudia aircraft; only Al Arabiya carries the ‘back to normal’ line. We have not found the GACA statement itself.

news.title: Saudi UN envoy: the Houthis targeted Riyadh airport in a blatant terrorist attack and threaten civil aviation
news.body: At the UN Security Council, Saudi Arabia’s envoy Abdulaziz Alwasil said the Houthi militia targeted Riyadh airport in a blatant terrorist attack, that its attacks wounded civilians including women and children, and (per Al Ekhbariya) that it threatens civil aviation security.

news.title: Al Ekhbariya: plans and preparations helped operations resume at King Khalid airport
news.body: Saudi state TV Al Ekhbariya’s correspondent said plans and preparations helped operations resume at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.

news.title: The United States condemns Houthi attacks on civilian infrastructure and airports in Saudi Arabia; the UK also backs the Kingdom
news.body: Saudi state TV Al Ekhbariya reports the United States condemned the Houthi attacks on civilian infrastructure and airports in the Kingdom and said it stands firmly with Saudi Arabia. At 6:09 PM it reported Britain also stands with the Kingdom and affirms its right to defend itself. Neither statement gives operational information.

news.title: Riyadh Airports tells passengers to check flight status with their airline
news.body: Replying to a passenger, the official Riyadh Airports account asked travellers to contact their airline to confirm flight status and get updates. It gave no reason for this afternoon’s stoppage.

news.title: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree says ‘humanitarian flights’ to and from Riyadh airport need a permit from Sanaa
news.body: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree posted that humanitarian flights to and from Riyadh airport will be allowed if they hold a permit from the humanitarian operations coordination centre in Sanaa. This confirms the statement was made, not that it has any effect on flights. The Houthis made no attack claim for Riyadh today.

news.title: Flightradar24: Riyadh airport ‘open again’
news.body: Flightradar24 posted that Riyadh airport was open again, four minutes after the first departure following the halt (Fly Jinnah 9P581 at 3:14 PM on the board). The cause of the 1:58 to 3:14 PM halt is UNCONFIRMED: GACA, KKIASA and Saudia have made no statement. A precautionary closure is likely but not confirmed.

news.title: Flightradar24: Riyadh airport ‘closed again’, no flights for an hour
news.extra: published 2:58 PM; last checked 8:45 PM; widely re-shared since, still no official reason as of 3:31 PM
news.body: Flightradar24 posted that Riyadh airport was closed again, with no landings or takeoffs in the past hour, and put today’s cancellations at 124, matching our board count. The cause is UNCONFIRMED: GACA, KKIASA and Saudia have made no statement. A precautionary closure is likely but not confirmed.

news.title: Social accounts report missile launches toward Riyadh and explosions around 2:05 PM; no official confirmation
news.extra: published 2:09 PM; last checked 8:45 PM; similar post 2:34 PM (https://x.com/dana916/status/2108521397412679740)
news.body: Several social accounts reported missile and drone launches from Yemen toward Riyadh at about 2:05 PM and explosions heard in the city, saying operations at King Khalid airport were suspended. GACA, Riyadh Airports and Saudia have not commented. The Flightradar24 board showed no movement from 1:58 to 3:14 PM (see section 1).
